text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert created — Elevated 5xx and timeout rates observed at the gateway since 12:03 UTC. Automations flagged a sustained increase in tail latencies and batch queue depth. Paging SRE-oncall.
carla: on it. joining. saw a ping from the alert. any customer-facing errors reported? :eyes:
eva: Cx reports some requests timing out, one large customer seeing 502s intermittently. Support page updated to 'investigating'.
dmitri: quick metric dump from the runtime dashboard:
```
metric: gateway.5xx_rate  -> 12:03 -> 12:11 spike from 0.2% to 6.8%
metric: scheduler.queue_depth -> 12:02 -> 12:10 increase from ~120 to 1400
metric: batching.head_of_line_blocks -> 12:04 -> 12:10 increase from 0 to 42
metric: kv_cache.evictions_per_min -> 12:06 -> 12:10 jump
```
maya: looking at the scheduler nodes — a subset (us-west-2-sched-3,4) show long GC pauses and many blocked batch workers. logs have repeated stack traces for batch_coordinator timeouts.
carla: is this a new deploy?
dmitri: no deploys in the last 24h. config change? autoscale?
infra-bot: autoscaler: no scale events in last 2h. GPU pool usage steady.
jordan: hypothesis: one noisy workload caused long-running batches that blocked the scheduler queue => head-of-line blocking, causing other requests to wait and hit timeouts/5xx.
eva: which customers are affected? I have tickets from AcmeCorp and BetaApps. both p95 and p99 elevated.
carla: ok, mitigation plan: 1) drain the two unhealthy scheduler nodes from routing, 2) force-evict oldest small batches to free slots, 3) temporarily disable large-batch routing for gateway callers, 4) if needed, fallback to single-request mode for high-priority customers. can demos be applied without full rollback?
maya: agree. I can mark us-west-2-sched-3,4 as draining in the routing table. command:
```
# mark sched nodes draining
rdctl routing set-drain --region us-west-2 --nodes us-west-2-sched-3,us-west-2-sched-4
```
carla: do it. also please reduce batch size target on gateway route to 1 for 10m window:
```
rdctl batching update --route gateway-prod --max-batch-size 1 --override-duration 10m
```
maya: applied both. confirmed routing removed new traffic from those sched nodes. batch target set to 1.
dmitri: running evictions now to clear queue:
```
schedulerctl evict --node us-west-2-sched-3 --policy oldest-first --limit 200
schedulerctl evict --node us-west-2-sched-4 --policy oldest-first --limit 200
```
infra-bot: eviction jobs started. progress: 200/200 on sched-3, 190/200 on sched-4.
jordan: metric watch: queue_depth dropping from 1400 -> 600 in last 4m. p99 latency improving slightly.
eva: notifying affected customers: AcmeCorp support updated: "We are actively mitigating an elevated error rate; temporary reduced throughput may occur. ETA 15-30m."
carla: thumbs up. also enable canary fallback to a lighter model for premium customers to avoid timeouts. maya, can you open a canary route?
maya: creating canary route gateway-prod-light with model-lite v1.2, route weight 0 initially. increasing to 30% for premium customer token buckets.
```
rdctl route create --name gateway-prod-light --model model-lite:v1.2 --weight 0
rdctl route weight --name gateway-prod-light --weight 30 --scope premium
```
maya: canary applied. traffic cutover started for premium tokens.
dmitri: seeing decreased 5xx on premium tokens, overall 5xx dropping from 6.8% -> 2.1% over 6m. still seeing some tail timeouts for non-premium.
carla: next steps: keep draining nodes, monitor for recurrence, plan restart of batch_coordinator on sched-3/4 during low traffic window if GC keeps happening. also create postmortem ticket.
jordan: note: root cause looks like a combination of a heavy request pattern that creates extremely long batch generation times + scheduler not preempting older batches => head-of-line. We should add preemption or max batch wall-time.
maya: logging suggests no preemption threshold set on those nodes. I can add a temporary wall-time of 3s to preempt long batches:
```
schedulerctl update-config --node-selector us-west-2 --max-batch-wall-ms 3000
```
maya: applied wall-time config; new batches will be preempted after 3s.
dmitri: metrics look stable over the next 8m: queue_depth ~120, gateway.5xx_rate ~0.6%, timeouts rare.
eva: customers confirmed degraded but improving. AcmeCorp upgraded their incident priority to 'monitoring'. no cancellations.
carla: handing off to next oncall in 20m for watch. summary for handoff: elevated gateway 5xx/timeouts caused by scheduler saturation/head-of-line blocking in us-west-2; drained two nodes, evicted oldest batches, reduced batch size to 1, enabled a lightweight model canary for premium traffic, applied max-batch-wall-time to preempt long-running batches. system appears stable.
carla: @dmitri @maya please file a postmortem and include a runbook entry for "head-of-line batching" with preemption defaults and autoscale triggers.
dmitri: filing PST-4821 with initial notes. linking diagnostic logs and commands used.
maya: I'll add a config change PR to set default max-batch-wall-ms=3000 for all scheduler pools and propose an incremental rollout.
carla: thanks. leaving oncall for 20m to monitor then handing off. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident 4135000123 status -> mitigated (recovery actions applied). Time to mitigation: 18m. Incident will be closed after postmortem.
eva: closing customer comms loop: updated AcmeCorp and BetaApps that issue mitigated and postmortem will follow.
dmitri: logs and metrics archived to PST-4821. moving to follow-up tasks.
carla: resolved. good job team. :tada:
